To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the scalar mesons are not conventional qq states, but rather they are four-quark states, and that the light scalar mesons are tetraquark states.
the scalar meson nonet is not a quarkonium state, but rather is a reflection of the QCD ground state.

(i) QCD sum rules are the best tool for relating quark dynamics to meson physics and for determining the nature of scalar mesons; (ii) lattice QCD is now sufficiently mature for the study of scalar mesons and other light-quark mesons; (iii) chiral perturbation theory, including the large-Nc limit, can be used to study the interactions of scalar mesons.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QCD vacuum is complex and rich in structure and that the mesons are a window on this structure.
the meson mass scale is not a fundamental scale of nature, but a scale which is set by the properties of the QCD ground state.
the quark model is alive and well, and that the study of hadrons is still an exciting field of physics.

we have a better idea of how to relate quark dynamics to low-energy hadron physics.
